channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao Senado por Rondônia em 2026
item.description: Rondônia will have 10 Senate candidates in the 2026 elections, with registration closing on August 15. A Real Time Big Data poll from July 15 shows Fernando Máximo (PL) leading with 19% voter intention, followed by Sílvia Cristina (PP) at 14%. The state has 1.27 million voters and is contesting two Senate seats.

item.title: Inelegível, Pablo Marçal registra candidatura a presidente pelo PRTB
item.description: Pablo Marçal's presidential candidacy for the 2026 elections was registered by the PRTB following a judicial injunction that regularized his party affiliation, despite his ineligibility. The registration was submitted to the TSE system but still requires final approval from the electoral court.

item.title: O verdadeiro motivo de Tereza Cristina não ter virado vice de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, president of the PP, initially backed Tereza Cristina as a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro but withdrew support after Federal Police investigations linked his allies to money laundering schemes involving banker Daniel Vorcaro, fearing police embarrassment before the election. He chose not to take the risk, despite having previously considered Nogueira as a likely vice and having given Tereza Cristina permission to seek internal party support.

item.title: Caiado descarta apoio a Lula no 2º turno após fala de Kassab
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD presidential candidate, ruled out any support for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in a potential runoff, reinforcing his long-standing opposition to the Workers' Party and stating his candidacy aims to remove the PT from power. The statement followed remarks by his running mate, Gilberto Kassab, who claimed Centrão parties are effectively aligned with Lula’s re-election. Caiado stressed there is no scenario in which he would support Lula, citing his four-decade political record, including leading the impeachment of Dilma Rousseff and reducing homicide rates in Goiás without leaving debt.

item.title: PRTB lança Pablo Marçal, que está inelegível, como candidato à Presidência
item.description: The PRTB filed Pablo Marçal's candidacy for President of Brazil, despite his legal ineligibility under electoral law. The party claims it obtained judicial authorization for his affiliation, but Marçal’s ineligibility remains a substantive barrier to his campaign. The move has sparked controversy, as Brazilian law prohibits individuals with final convictions or other disqualifying conditions from running for elected office.

item.title: Pablo Marçal, que está inelegível, registra candidatura à Presidência
item.description: Pablo Marçal, the PRTB candidate who is currently ineligible, registered his presidential candidacy with the TSE following a provisional injunction that allowed his temporary affiliation with the party. The registration took place on Saturday (August 15) and marks a twist in the presidential race, as his ineligibility remains under judicial review.

item.title: Ao conquistar os líderes do Centrão, um a um, risco de Lula é um novo ‘petrolão’
item.description: By securing support from Centrão figures such as Ciro Nogueira, Davi Alcolumbre, and Hugo Motta, President Lula strengthens his congressional base and re-election prospects in 2026, yet repeats the pattern that led to the mensalão and Petrolão scandals. This pragmatic, non-ideological alliance strategy involves concessions to regional and sectoral interests, risking quid-pro-quo arrangements that could compromise Petrobras and governance. The cost, the text argues, is borne by society, reviving a cycle of institutional corruption in the name of political survival.

item.title: 49,9% dos candidatos de 2026 se declaram negros; 48,6%, brancos
item.description: In the 2026 elections, 49.9% of the 10,200 candidates self-declared as Black, representing a 0.4 percentage point decrease from the 50.3% recorded in 2022. The figure includes 7,412 pardos (mixed-race) and 2,788 pretos (Black) candidates, based on preliminary TSE data released after the August 15, 2026 registration deadline. Despite the decline, the policy requiring parties to allocate at least 30% of campaign funds to Black and mixed-race candidatures remains in effect since 2024.

item.title: Candidaturas femininas são 34,8% nas Eleições de 2026
item.description: Women account for 34.8% of candidacies in Brazil's 2026 General Elections, a new proportional record, up one percentage point from the 2022 presidential election. In absolute numbers, there will be 13,320 male candidates and 7,116 female candidates, despite women comprising 51.5% of Brazil's population according to the 2022 IBGE Census.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao governo de São Paulo em 2026
item.description: São Paulo will have 7 candidates for governor in 2026, with Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) seeking re-election and Fernando Haddad (PT) as his main rival. A Meio/Ideia poll from August 10 shows Tarcísio leading with 51% voting intention, compared to Haddad's 34%, suggesting a potential first-round victory. Candidate registration closed on August 15, 2026, and candidate data is publicly accessible via Políticos do Brasil and Poder Drive.

item.title: Rui Costa Pimenta declara ao TSE não possuir bens
item.description: Rui Costa Pimenta, presidential candidate for the PCO, declared to the TSE that he owns no assets when registering his candidacy. Hertz Dias of the PSTU made the same declaration. Asset disclosure is mandatory for candidacy registration and aims to ensure transparency.

item.title: Caiado diz que não apoiará Lula após fala de Kassab sobre Centrão
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) stated he will not support Lula in any electoral scenario, emphasizing his historical opposition to the PT since 1989. The declaration followed criticism from his running mate, Gilberto Kassab (PSD), who claimed the Centrão is not neutral and backs Lula’s re-election, while calling Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) chances 'zero'. Caiado said his campaign aims to remove the PT from power and position itself as a right-wing alternative independent of Bolsonarism.

item.title: Vanderlan Cardoso (PSD) declara patrimônio de R$ 66 milhões; veja patrimônio de candidato ao Senado em Goiás
item.description: PSD Senate candidate Vanderlan Cardoso from Goiás declared R$ 66.8 million in assets to the TSE, with major holdings including private credit (R$ 24.5 million), aircraft shares (R$ 13.3 million), and an R$ 8.3 million residence. This reflects a 149.28% increase from his 2024 mayoral candidacy in Goiânia, when he declared R$ 26.8 million. The disclosure highlights significant wealth concentration in financial and high-value real assets.

item.title: Justiça proíbe suspeito de se aproximar de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A court in Minas Gerais barred a suspect accused of threatening Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from coming within 500 meters of the lawmaker, his residence, workplace, and campaign activities. The restraining order was issued following an investigation into threats against the presidential candidate.

item.title: Polícia do Senado identifica suspeito de ameaçar Flávio em Minas
item.description: The Senate Legislative Police and Minas Gerais Civil Police executed a search and seizure warrant in Juiz de Fora (MG) against a man suspected of threatening presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro with violent Facebook comments. The suspect, who has eight prior records for assault and threats, was taken in for questioning, had electronic devices seized, and was barred from coming within 500 meters of the candidate. The operation takes place amid heightened alert, as Juiz de Fora was the site of the knife attack on Jair Bolsonaro in 2018.

item.title: Lula prepara ato de campanha com slogan “O Brasil pronto pra mais”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will launch his 2026 re-election campaign on August 16, 2026, at 9 a.m., at the Estádio 1º de Maio in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), unveiling the slogan 'Brazil ready for more'. The event, expected to draw 20,000 attendees, will highlight government achievements in social programs, national defense, rare earth exploration, and full-time education, while attacking PL candidate Flávio Bolsonaro for alleged alignment with Donald Trump.

item.title: Presidenciáveis declaram patrimônios de R$ 33 mil a R$ 242 milhões
item.description: Presidential candidates in Brazil's 2026 election declared assets ranging from R$33,000 to R$242.2 million, according to TSE data. Augusto Cury (Avante) leads with R$242.2 million, followed by Romeu Zema (Novo) at R$178.7 million and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) at R$52.5 million. Hertz Dias (PSTU) and Rui Costa Pimenta (PCO) declared no assets.

item.title: Candidato do PCB à Presidência declara R$ 454,5 mil em bens
item.description: PCB presidential candidate Edmilson Costa declared R$ 454,485.68 in assets to the TSE, a 9.5% decrease from 2014 when he ran for Senate. His running mate, Cleusa Santos, reported R$ 1.79 million, a 16.2% increase from 2024. The figures come from the DivulgaCandContas system, with candidate registration closing on Saturday (Aug 15, 2026).

item.title: Polícia do Senado cumpre mandado contra suspeito de ameaçar Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Senate Police executed a search and seizure warrant in Juiz de Fora (MG) against a suspect accused of threatening Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on social media. The threat was identified by the Senate’s Intelligence Situation Room during monitoring of risks to campaigning legislators. The suspect gave testimony, seized materials will undergo forensic analysis, and the case has been referred to the Minas Gerais Public Prosecutor’s Office.

item.title: Campanha presidencial pega fogo, mas ainda não comove os eleitores
item.description: The 2026 presidential race is fiercely contested between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with both technically tied in second-round simulations (43% to 40%), despite scandals involving the Master Bank scheme and alleged looting of INSS pension funds. Despite high media coverage, most voters remain disengaged: 51% do not name a candidate spontaneously, 41% are unaware of the Bolsonaro family reconciliation, and 29% of independents say they will not vote.

item.title: Tatuador é detido suspeito de ameaçar esfaquear Flávio em Juiz de Fora (MG)
item.description: Lauro Cesar Costa Junior, a 41-year-old tattoo artist, was detained in Juiz de Fora (MG) on suspicion of threatening to stab Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who has a scheduled agenda in the city next Monday. The incident occurred in the same municipality where Jair Bolsonaro was stabbed during the 2018 election campaign. Authorities are investigating the motive and credibility of the threat.

item.title: Cleitinho sobre 3 caminhonetes declaradas ao TSE: "São para trabalho"
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) declared three pickup trucks valued at R$ 518,9 thousand to the TSE, representing 54.2% of his total declared assets of R$ 956.5 thousand, stating they are used for work and citing security reasons for not showing them. His assets grew 76% since 2022, driven by replacing two older vehicles with a Ram Rampage and Ford Maverick, increasing vehicle value from R$ 157.8 thousand to R$ 518.9 thousand. He also claimed his campaign will be the 'cheapest in Brazil'.

item.title: Homem suspeito de ameaçar Flávio Bolsonaro é levado à delegacia em MG
item.description: A man suspected of threatening Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a presidential candidate, was taken to a police station in Juiz de Fora (MG) after posting a social media message with knife emojis and the phrase "this time leave it to me", referencing the candidate’s upcoming visit to the city where Jair Bolsonaro was stabbed in 2018. The Senate Legislative Police activated the Minas Gerais Public Prosecutor’s Office and obtained judicial authorization for electronic device searches and protective measures, including a 500-meter exclusion zone around the candidate and his campaign/work locations.

item.title: Após ameaça, campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro fala em ação ágil da Polícia e destaca episódio de 2018
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign praised the swift action of the Senate Legislative Police in identifying a man who threatened the candidate with a stabbing on social media, recalling the 2018 stabbing attack on Jair Bolsonaro. The suspect was taken in for questioning in Juiz de Fora (MG), where the 2018 attack occurred, and had his residence targeted by a search and seizure warrant with support from Minas Gerais Civil Police. Flávio Bolsonaro has a campaign event scheduled in the city next Monday (17).

item.title: Candidatos de 2026 declaram R$ 136 milhões em aviões e barcos
item.description: Candidates in the 2026 elections declared R$136.1 million in aircraft and boats by 3:30 p.m. on August 15, according to preliminary TSE data compiled by Poder360. Senator Vanderlan Cardoso (PSD-GO) leads with R$25.3 million in aerial assets, including 11.11% of a plane valued at R$13.3 million and full ownership of another worth R$11.9 million. The figures are subject to change due to incomplete or erroneous filings, but updates are not expected to materially affect the report’s analysis.

item.title: Com quatro fortunas acima de R$ 50 milhões, veja o patrimônio de todos os candidatos à Presidência da República
item.description: Four presidential candidates in Brazil's 2026 election declared assets over R$ 50 million, led by writer Augusto Cury (Avante) with R$ 242.28 million and former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) with R$ 178.7 million. The figures were adjusted for inflation from August 2022 to July 2026. Cury's wealth is mainly from loans (R$ 128.51 million) and business holdings, while Zema runs under the Novo party.

item.title: Rui Costa Pimenta declara não ter patrimônio ao TSE
item.description: Rui Costa Pimenta, PCO’s presidential candidate, declared zero assets when registering his candidacy with the TSE on August 15, 2026, which is legally permissible if no intentional omission of property exists. While declaring no assets is allowed under electoral law, intentional concealment of wealth constitutes the crime of ideological falsity in electoral context. Pimenta, a long-time leader of the PCO and former PT militant, previously ran for president in 2002, 2010, and 2014.

item.title: Inelegível, Pablo Marçal consegue liminar para voltar ao PRTB
item.description: Electoral Court Judge Gustavo Nardi granted a provisional injunction allowing Pablo Marçal to rejoin the PRTB party, enabling him to run for President of Brazil under that ticket. The ruling is retroactive, overriding his March affiliation with União Brasil. Despite being deemed ineligible by some interpretations, Marçal is seeking to revive his presidential bid.

item.title: O candidato à Presidência que promete botox gratuito para as mulheres
item.description: Presidential candidate Wilson Grassi, a veterinarian and former doorman, promises free Botox for Brazilian women through his 'Meu Botox, Minha Vida' program, claiming it boosts self-esteem and productivity. To fund the initiative, he proposes closing ministries such as Culture and reallocating funds from the Special Campaign Financing Fund, which distributes nearly R$5 billion to parties each election. Grassi, who has pursued politics for over two decades, has previously run for state deputy, federal congressman, and city councilor without success.

item.title: Jucá registra candidatura a deputado federal após decisões judiciais
item.description: Former senator Romero Jucá (MDB-RR) registered his candidacy for federal deputy from Roraima following provisional decisions by the STF and STJ that suspended the effects of his conviction for passive corruption and money laundering, linked to R$150,000 received from Odebrecht in 2014. Minister Flávio Dino (STF) ordered the case be returned to the Supreme Court, as the alleged crimes occurred during his senatorial mandate, while Minister Messod Azulay Neto (STJ) ruled the conviction does not bar him from running while the case is under review. Jucá, a three-term senator and former minister in the Lula and Temer administrations, had his candidacy registered, but it remains subject to final approval by the Electoral Justice.

item.title: Caiado declara mais de R$ 52 milhões ao TSE
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, presidential candidate for PSD-GO, declared R$ 52.557.930,98 in assets to the TSE, highlighting livestock (R$ 10.4 million) and other real estate (R$ 36.2 million). His government plan, presented with running mate Gilberto Kassab, proposes ending presidential reelection and adopting a mixed-district system for legislative elections.

item.title: De R$ 33 mil a R$ 242 mi: veja patrimônio declarado por presidenciáveis
item.description: Presidential candidates in the 2026 Brazilian elections declared assets ranging from R$33,000 to R$242.28 million, according to TSE data. This wide disparity highlights significant financial differences among those running for the nation's highest office.

item.title: Arruda declara R$ 830 mil; vice de sua chapa registra R$ 26,2 milhões
item.description: José Roberto Arruda (PSD), candidate for Governor of the Federal District in 2026, declared R$ 830,2 thousand in assets, a modest increase since 2022, while his running mate, Luiz Pitiman (PSD), declared R$ 26.2 million, revealing a significant wealth disparity in the ticket. Arruda has a history of administrative misconduct convictions, including being ordered to repay R$ 595 million to public coffers linked to Operation Pandora's Box, and is seeking to enable his candidacy despite ineligibility, relying on proposed changes to the Clean Record Law under discussion at the STF.

item.title: Suspeito de ameaçar Flávio é alvo de busca e apreensão em Juiz de Fora
item.description: A resident of Juiz de Fora (MG) was targeted in a search and seizure operation after being investigated for allegedly threatening Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a 2026 presidential candidate. He was taken in for testimony. The investigation began following a social media post.

item.title: Programas de Lula e Flávio fazem promessas sem dizer como vão bancar gastos
item.description: The government programs of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) contain numerous promises but fail to explain how they will finance the expenditures, according to economists analyzed by Folha.

item.title: Governo Lula pressiona Alcolumbre por fim da 6x1 antes das eleições
item.description: The Lula government intensified efforts to approve before the October elections a constitutional amendment ending the 6×1 work schedule, following three meetings between the president and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. The PEC, already passed by the Chamber of Deputies, had been stalled in the Senate but had its unblocking announced on Friday (Aug 14) after a meeting at the Alvorada Palace. Alcolumbre, who previously resisted political-electoral pressure, signaled a shift in stance amid rapprochement with the Planalto Palace.

item.title: Zema: “Contra o PT voto até num copo”
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) stated he would vote for any candidate facing the PT in a potential 2026 presidential runoff. He hopes to receive support from other right-wing candidates if he advances to the second round. His remarks emphasize his ideological opposition to the PT, even if it means backing less-than-ideal alternatives.

item.title: Tarcísio dará pontapé inicial na campanha eleitoral com mulheres em Osasco
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) will kick off his 2026 electoral campaign with a women's roundtable in Osasco, SP, this Friday (16). The event will bring together homemakers, entrepreneurs, and community leaders to discuss their expectations for the state government over the next four years. The initiative highlights a strategic focus on social and gender issues in his campaign approach.

item.title: Ex-presidente do PSB cobra esquerda por mais repressão ao crime organizado
item.description: Former PSB president Carlos Siqueira argues that the left must reassess its public security policies, advocating for firmer repression against organized crime while maintaining social policies that address its root causes. He emphasizes that precarious youth, mothers heads of household, and evangelicals — groups feeling abandoned by the state — seek security as a response to institutional neglect. Concern over violence already dominates the pre-electoral debate, even before the official campaign begins.

item.title: 'Lula se apequenou em processo', diz Flávio sobre tarifas de reciprocidade contra EUA
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) criticized President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), calling him irresponsible after the start of a process that could lead to the application of the Economic Reciprocity Law against the U.S. Flávio claimed Lula 'diminished himself' by adopting reciprocal tariff measures, which he views as harmful to Brazil's economy and inappropriate amid ongoing trade tensions with the United States.

item.title: Empate técnico marca início da disputa presidencial entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro, aponta Quaest
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are technically tied at 43% and 40% respectively in a potential runoff, with a two-point margin of error, according to Quaest poll. The tie reflects a return to pre-May revelation levels, when Lula had an eight-point lead over Bolsonaro’s son. In the first-round scenario, Lula leads with 38% to Flávio’s 31%, with the senator’s recovery driven by Southeast voters, evangelicals, and independents.

item.title: Quaest: os grupos em que a disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro está mais apertada
item.description: The Quaest poll shows a technical tie between Lula (43%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (40%) in the 2026 runoff, with the difference within the margin of error. Lula leads among youth (16-34), Northeast, low income, Black voters, and Catholics, while Flávio wins among men, South, evangelicals, and high income. Independent voters (33% of the electorate) favor Flávio (35% vs 29%), and women lean toward Lula (44% vs 35%).

item.title: Amiga de Lulinha ainda luta para ter acesso a inquéritos no STF
item.description: Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of Lulinha (President Lula’s son) under investigation for influence peddling, still has not gained access to the STF inquiries, despite her messages with businessman ‘Careca do INSS’ and Lula’s son being central to the investigations. She is also linked to a R$249,000 payment to Lula’s former chief of staff, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), who claims it was a repaid loan. The case involves two STF rapporteurs — Flávio Dino and André Mendonça — due to the separate inquiries into Lulinha’s alleged scheme.

item.title: Proporção de editoriais críticos ao STF sobe em 4 jornais
item.description: The proportion of editorials critical of the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF) increased in the first half of 2026 across four major newspapers, with Folha de S.Paulo showing the largest rise at 15.14 percentage points. The Ranking dos Políticos analyzed 1,833 editorials from 2023 to June 2026, finding that criticism focused on monocratic decisions, the Banco Master case, and perceived power concentration. Despite the rise in criticism, outlets like O Globo and Folha acknowledged the STF’s role in defending democracy and institutions.

item.title: Vice-campeã do BBB 17, Vivian Amorim sai candidata e expõe bens ao TSE
item.description: Vivian Amorim, runner-up of BBB 17 and member of the União Brasil party, is running for federal deputy from Amazonas, having declared a net worth of R$ 3.4 million to the TSE. She owns two residential properties (in São Paulo and Manaus), over R$ 768,000 in investment funds, R$ 100,000 in her individual company’s capital, and bank balances, in addition to earning R$ 150,000 during the reality show. The article highlights how she leveraged her BBB fame to build wealth and enter politics.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Candidatos à Presidência declaram patrimônios que variam de R$ 30 mil a R$ 242 milhões ao TSE
item.description: The asset declarations of presidential candidates to the TSE reveal extreme wealth disparity, ranging from R$ 33,000 (Samara Martins, UP) to R$ 242 million (Augusto Cury, Avante). Cury leads with assets driven by loans, corporate holdings, and stocks, followed by Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD). Declarations are mandatory for candidacy registration and publicly accessible via DivulgaCand.

item.title: Tarcísio dará pontapé inicial na campanha eleitoral com roda de conversa com mulheres em Osasco
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas launches his 2026 electoral campaign with a women's forum in Osasco, aiming to boost his support among female voters, as polls show 50% male support versus 34% female support. The event highlights proposals for 24-hour women's police stations and phase-specific health programs, while signaling an initial focus on the São Paulo metropolitan region, where his main rival Haddad outperformed him in 2022.

item.title: ‘Lula se apequenou em processo’, diz Flávio sobre tarifas de reciprocidade contra EUA
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) accused President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) of having 'diminished himself' in the process of applying the Economic Reciprocity Law in response to U.S. tariffs on Brazilian steel and aluminum. He claimed Lula acted irresponsibly by provoking the U.S. and is now focused only on re-election, not national interest. Flávio also denounced a alleged fraudulent affiliation with the Missão party, claiming he was a victim of an electoral crime.

item.title: Governo Lula ganha fôlego para o Orçamento, mas ajuste em 2027 segue inevitável, dizem economistas
item.description: The Lula administration has secured temporary room to finalize the 2026 Annual Budget Bill (PLOA) by the August 31 deadline, following recent revenue and expenditure adjustments. However, economists warn that structural fiscal adjustment remains inevitable in 2027 due to persistent spending pressures and primary deficit targets.

item.title: Renan Santos relata ameaça de morte e aciona Polícia Federal
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) reported receiving a death threat detailing a plan to shoot him on August 16, 2026, the date of his official campaign launch at Largo de São Francisco in São Paulo. The anonymous message, allegedly from a USP law student, claims he purchased an illegal firearm on the dark web and labels Santos a 'Nazi' and 'Brazil's top fascist leader' as justification. Despite the threat, Santos affirmed the event will proceed with heightened police presence and confirmed he has filed a report with the Federal Police.
